reviewMethod.methodNotesMd: Reviewed the SearchParameter StructureDefinition diff, the direct SearchParameters behavior findings whose `affectedResources` include `SearchParameter`, and the shared Resource/DomainResource behavior findings as context only. I used the deterministic aggregate only after forming the resource-level conclusion.

r4Maturity.effectMd: SearchParameter was trial-use/FMM 3 in R4. That is not a normative freeze, but it creates meaningful stability pressure because SearchParameter resources are executable conformance metadata used by validators, registries, generated clients, CapabilityStatement comparisons, and server indexing.

overall.oneLineConclusion: SearchParameter keeps its identity but needs a targeted R4-to-R6 migration program for search conformance metadata; low-cost compatibility preservation still has high value.

reasoning.thesisMd: The resource is not removed or replaced, and much of the model remains recognizable. However, R6 changes the executable metadata rules enough that importing real R4 SearchParameter catalogs unchanged is not viable: XPath fields disappear, `expression` now requires `processingMode`, required-bound resource type and modifier code domains change, and additional hard invariants reject some old definitions. This is a targeted conformance-metadata migration, not a wholesale resource replacement.
reasoning.migrationShapeMd: The dominant migration work is policy/tooling for SearchParameter registries: remove or preserve legacy `xpath`/`xpathUsage`, populate `processingMode`, normalize `ofType` to `of-type` if R6 does not retain an alias, validate `base` and `target` against the version-independent resource-type set, and account for newly enforced URL-safe `code` and comparator rules. The changes are concentrated in search-definition semantics rather than ordinary patient/clinical instance data.
reasoning.compatibilityLeverageMd: A migration program is already unavoidable for serious SearchParameter publishers, but that does not make additional breaks low value. Several breaks appear cheap to soften in the base standard with deprecated fields, aliases, default semantics, lifecycle-marked resource codes, or canonical SearchParameter aliases. Those measures would reduce validator, generator, and registry churn while still letting R6 move toward the cleaner model.
reasoning.lessBreakingAlternativesMd: The strongest preservation candidates are retaining deprecated `xpath`/`xpathUsage`, treating absent `processingMode` as `normal` or warning-level for one release, retaining `ofType` as a deprecated modifier alias, and ensuring the version-independent resource-type value set really includes R4 resource codes with lifecycle metadata. By contrast, the comparator and URL-safe code invariants look more like local cleanup chores once migration is accepted because they address misleading or ambiguous metadata and appear rare in core R4 content.
reasoning.behaviorImpactMd: The direct SearchParameters behavior findings reinforce the same conclusion. The `ofType` to `of-type` rename is both a StructureDefinition required-binding break and a public search API/codegen surface break. The CanonicalResource/MetadataResource consolidation preserves many runtime query codes but changes canonical SearchParameter identity, which is important for CapabilityStatement definitions, conformance tests, generated clients, and registries. Shared Resource/DomainResource behavior findings remain background context only for this review.
reasoning.comparisonToDeterministicAggregateMd: The deterministic aggregate concluded `Partial`, `moderate-targeted-remodel`, and `preserve-where-low-cost-but-expect-resource-migration`. I agree with that posture, but the reason is not just the count of six hard breaks: it is the combination of common catalog-level invalidation, required-code/domain changes, and direct behavior identity changes, with several plausible low-cost compatibility mechanisms still available.
reasoning.uncertaintyMd: Confidence is high for the local structural and direct behavior shape. Residual uncertainty is mainly terminology-specific: the exact official expansion and intended lifecycle semantics of `version-independent-all-resource-types` should be confirmed with an authoritative terminology service or standards rationale. The R6 input is ballot4, so details may still change.

findingConsiderations.title: SearchParameter.xpath and SearchParameter.xpathUsage were removed in R6
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This is the clearest model migration. R4 has optional `xpath` and required-bound `xpathUsage` metadata that appear widely in core SearchParameter resources; R6 removes both and introduces `processingMode`. That makes unchanged R4 definitions invalid or lossy, but retaining deprecated optional XPath fields would be a plausible low-cost transition.

findingConsiderations.title: R6 requires processingMode whenever expression is present
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: The new error invariant creates a mass old-valid/new-invalid pattern for R4 definitions with `expression` but no `processingMode`. The R6 goal of explicit processing semantics is reasonable, but a default of `normal` or a warning-level transition would preserve most R4 catalogs with little semantic cost.

findingConsiderations.title: Search modifier code ofType was renamed to of-type and new modifier codes were added
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: `SearchParameter.modifier` is required-bound and search modifiers are part of public query metadata. The additive R6 codes are not the problem; dropping the R4 `ofType` spelling is an avoidable wire-code break where a deprecated alias would likely preserve compatibility at modest cost.

findingConsiderations.title: SearchParameter.base and target changed to a version-independent resource-type binding that is not a simple R4 superset
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: `base` and `target` remain required-bound resource-type codes, so differences in the value set can reject otherwise valid R4 SearchParameters. Because the R6 value set is described as version-independent, missing R4 resource codes are standards-review-worthy unless intentionally covered by lifecycle semantics.

findingConsiderations.title: R6 forbids comparator unless type is number, date, quantity, or special
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This is a real hard validation break, but it appears rare in core R4 content and prevents misleading comparator declarations on unordered search parameter types. Once the broader SearchParameter migration is accepted, this is mostly a local cleanup rule rather than a reason to change the resource-level posture.

findingConsiderations.title: R6 rejects SearchParameter.code values containing '.', '$', '|', or whitespace
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This can break custom R4 SearchParameters, but the prohibited characters are meaningful separators in FHIR search syntax and no core R4 examples were found. It is worth documenting and tooling, but less compelling as a standards reversal than the alias/default/resource-type issues.

findingConsiderations.title: SearchParameter.type added R6-only code resource
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: Adding `resource` widens the R6 type code set and does not invalidate R4 SearchParameter instances. It is primarily an R6-to-R4 downgrade or generated-enum update concern, so it should not drive R4-to-R6 break-avoidance.

findingConsiderations.title: R6 adds SearchParameter.constraint for conditional applicability
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: The new `constraint` element is optional and does not reject R4 instances. R4 consumers may lose this R6-only metadata on downgrade, but that is not a problematic R4-to-R6 break.

findingConsiderations.title: R6 adds optional canonical metadata and alias fields not present in R4
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: The added canonical metadata and alias fields are optional. They may need extension-based preservation when downgrading to R4, but they do not create an R4-to-R6 instance break.

findingConsiderations.title: R6 gives SearchParameter.chain special wildcard, unlimited, and dotted-path semantics
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: `chain` remains a repeatable string, and the issue is mainly new R6 semantics for special string forms. Existing R4 chain values remain structurally valid, so this is not a major R4-to-R6 migration driver.

findingConsiderations.title: SearchParameter.modifier code `ofType` was replaced by `of-type` while new modifiers were added
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: The behavior report confirms the structure finding has runtime/API/codegen consequences: custom SearchParameter resources, validators, query builders, and generated enums can contain or expect `ofType`. This makes the deprecated-alias alternative especially valuable.

findingConsiderations.title: R6 consolidates many per-resource canonical SearchParameter URLs into multi-base CanonicalResource and MetadataResource definitions
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: Runtime query codes often survive, but canonical SearchParameter URLs are conformance identities. This is avoidable with deprecated aliases or equivalence guidance and matters for SearchParameter registries, CapabilityStatement.searchParam.definition, generated clients, and conformance tests.

findingConsiderations.title: Resource $meta-add is removed from R6 core
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This shared Resource-level operation removal may affect systems that operate on SearchParameter instances generically, but the review instructions classify Resource/DomainResource behavior as context only unless the assigned artifact is Resource or DomainResource. It therefore does not change the SearchParameter resource-level conclusion.

findingConsiderations.title: Core special/profile search parameters changed type metadata for _content, _text, _query, and _profile
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This shared search behavior can affect generic Resource/DomainResource search handling, but it is not a direct SearchParameter finding in this assigned review. It remains useful background for search tooling migration, not a scored SearchParameter-specific break.

recommendedNextActions.actionMd: Ask the standards group to review low-cost compatibility options for the four core `Revisit` structure breaks: deprecated `xpath`/`xpathUsage`, absent-`processingMode` default or warning transition, deprecated `ofType` alias, and lifecycle-complete version-independent resource-type bindings.

Publish explicit R4-to-R6 SearchParameter migration guidance and tests for registry imports: XPath metadata handling, `processingMode` population, modifier normalization, `base`/`target` code validation, comparator pruning, and URL-safe code checks.

For CanonicalResource/MetadataResource consolidation, provide canonical URL alias/equivalence guidance so CapabilityStatement comparisons and generated clients can match old per-resource SearchParameter definitions to the new multi-base definitions.
Confirm `version-independent-all-resource-types` behavior with an authoritative terminology expansion and document how retired, renamed, or version-specific R4 resource codes should be represented.

caveats: The R6 source package is 6.0.0-ballot4, not a final release.
Terminology conclusions for resource-type bindings are based on local package data rather than an authoritative terminology-server expansion.
Prevalence statements are based on core package SearchParameter resources and may understate custom IG or production registry usage.
Shared Resource/DomainResource behavior findings were considered only as context, per the review instructions.
